interpretationModel.engineeringEquivalentDefinition: The existing CODEX EXECUTION AND ITERATION, USER REVIEW AND DECISION, and MANUAL EXTERNAL WORK hours are engineering-equivalent effort allocations. They are not literal user stopwatch time and CODEX EXECUTION AND ITERATION is not literal Codex wall-clock runtime.
interpretationModel.userAttendedDefinition: Active user participation for prompt launch, blocker answers, report/diff review, manual checks, acceptance, authorization, wallet/DNS/production/rollback decisions, and commits. USER-CHECK-IN TIME is included and not counted separately.
interpretationModel.unattendedWallClockDefinition: Planning range for primary/fix Codex runs and routine scripts, builds, downloads, browser automation, screenshot suites, validation, and deploy verification that can progress without continuous user attention. It is wall-clock, not labor.
interpretationModel.passiveElapsedDefinition: External or queue waiting such as DNS/cache/certificate/deploy propagation, monitoring-window duration, service delays, and exceptional CI/browser queueing. Routine tool execution is represented once in unattended wall-clock; passive notes are non-additive elapsed dependencies.
interpretationModel.conversionMethod: Each ticket was reviewed using its user-review and manual-external hours, pass pattern, confidence, complexity, and authorization/manual gates. Attended time retains active decisions, review, checks, approvals, wallet/DNS/rollback actions, and commits; it discounts overlap, witness-only time, non-continuous monitoring, agent-led status work, and conservative engineering allowance. Shared practical prompt/launch/check-in/commit overhead is added once at 0.5/1.0/1.5 hours per included ticket for low/expected/high milestones; ticket practicalTime excludes it.
caveats: Practical attended conversion has lower confidence than the engineering-equivalent model because work habits, review depth, authorization friction, and failure frequency are not yet observed.
Attended and unattended ranges are planning aids, not guarantees, and are not added to engineering-equivalent labor.
Unattended execution is serialized by the one-ticket-at-a-time workflow and still requires brief check-ins captured inside user-attended time.
Routine build/test/browser execution is included in unattended wall-clock; external queues, propagation, monitoring duration, and service waiting remain passive elapsed dependencies.
No calendar duration follows by summing the clocks because activity can overlap and passive dependencies are state-based.

estimationModel.workflow: One scoped Codex ticket at a time; optimized prompt before execution; Codex inspects, implements, validates and reports; user reviews, witnesses/executes required manual checks, resolves decisions and commits; ordinary fix passes are expected; no autonomous multi-ticket run.

laborCategories.codexExecutionAndIteration: Active scoped-session time for investigation, implementation, interpreting validation, correction, and expected targeted fix passes.
laborCategories.userReviewAndDecision: Completion-report and result review, decisions, blocked answers, witnessed checks, approval, and commit/continuity work.
laborCategories.manualExternalWork: Browser, authorization, provenance/licensing, DNS/domain, wallet, approved Shadownet, visual acceptance, monitoring and rollback work that Codex cannot independently complete.
laborCategories.passiveMachineTime: Unattended builds, downloads, screenshot/browser suites, deploy propagation, DNS/cache waiting and monitoring-window elapsed duration.

estimationModel.lowDefinition: Evidence/access available; first implementation substantially correct; no material architecture surprise; one normal review cycle.
estimationModel.expectedDefinition: One primary Codex pass, one focused review, ordinary correction/fix work and expected browser/manual checks; no architecture reversal. Expected is judgment-based, not automatically the midpoint.
estimationModel.highDefinition: Multiple fix passes, difficult browser/CSS/environment behavior, external friction, and one material but contained surprise; no fundamental architecture replacement.
estimationModel.passiveTimeTreatment: Excluded from every labor total; only active monitoring, interpretation, retry, or decision time is counted.

practicalTime.passiveElapsedNotes: Access/authorization waits and exceptional browser or download queueing are passive; routine tool execution is already in unattended wall-clock.

minimumFoundation.excluded: Deployment pipeline, full functional/visual closure, staging, production, monitoring closeout, Webflow decommission, optional cleanup.

workflowOverhead.basis: Per included ticket: 1.0/1.5/2.0 hours for prompt refinement, branch/status continuity, commit handling, blocked-question resolution, and dependency handoff. Ticket-specific implementation, completion-report review, and fix passes remain in ticket estimates; passive machine time is excluded.

scenarios.name: EXPECTED CASE
basis: Ordinary asset/font verification and CSS localization
One or two widget/runtime fix passes

scenarios.name: DIFFICULT BUT CONTAINED CASE
basis: Additional asset acquisition and font metric adjustment
Page-specific CSS drift and multiple Tabs/first-paint fixes
Contained static-host adjustment without architecture replacement

scenarios.name: ARCHITECTURE-INVALIDATING CASE
basis: Transaction runtime requires rewrite against generated DOM
Required assets cannot be hosted legally or technically
Static hosting cannot meet route behavior

alternatives.name: FULL RECOMMENDED MIGRATION

practicalUserAttended.interpretation: Same practical safe-independence clock as the selected program.

alternatives.scopePoint: Through safe Webflow independence; optional cleanup is separate.
alternatives.retainedWebflowDependencies: Baseline and rollback only until closure; none operational after approved decommission.
alternatives.maintenanceImpact: Lowest long-term source duplication; generated HTML remains reproducible.
alternatives.risk: Medium implementation risk, concentrated in assets/fonts, CSS/visual parity, runtime seams and cutover.

alternatives.name: MINIMAL DEPENDENCY REDUCTION

practicalUserAttended.interpretation: Fewer tickets and external cutover gates, but active review of selected runtime/first-paint changes remains.

alternatives.scopePoint: Selective Git bundle and first-paint hardening while Webflow hosting/HTML/CMS/presentation remain.
alternatives.retainedWebflowDependencies: Hosting, HTML, CMS, CSS, assets/fonts, widgets and deployment remain.
alternatives.maintenanceImpact: Continues split ownership and Webflow publishing dependence; does not deliver independence.
alternatives.risk: Low-to-medium change risk but high retained platform/ownership risk.
alternatives.recommendation: Use only if the independence objective is deferred; not a substitute for the accepted architecture.

alternatives.name: SNAPSHOT-BASED PARTIAL MIGRATION

practicalUserAttended.interpretation: Lower implementation breadth than full generation but substantial manual HTML, visual, asset/font, hosting and cutover review remains.

alternatives.scopePoint: Use checked HTML as long-term source, reconstruct Collection Utility, and localize CSS/assets/fonts without canonical template/data generation.
benefits: Faster path to static hosting than full generation
alternatives.retainedWebflowDependencies: Can remove runtime fetching, but preserves Webflow-derived duplicated HTML as the authoring model and baseline provenance.
alternatives.maintenanceImpact: Manual edits across duplicated rows/shells and weak content-source consistency; 66 item-route maintenance remains awkward.
alternatives.risk: Medium-to-high long-term drift and regression risk despite lower expected initial labor.
alternatives.recommendation: Viable fallback only if structured generation proves disproportionately difficult; current evidence does not justify overriding WF-MIG.6.

invalidatingConditions: Current published behavior depends on undiscovered server-side functionality.
Live CMS authoring is a post-migration requirement rather than Git-based content updates.
Existing wallet/transaction runtime cannot operate against generated contract-preserving DOM without a material rewrite.
Required assets or fonts cannot legally or technically be independently hosted and no approved equivalent exists.
No static host can reproduce required direct, nested-item, unknown-path, TLS, cache and rollback behavior.
A critical inaccessible IX2 interaction or other Webflow-only runtime behavior is discovered.
The route, CMS item, asset, responsive-state or browser matrix is materially larger than the committed audit evidence.
